clauses.clause: Sole clause: EO 1084 (1909-06-08) and EO 1096 (1909-06-25), four-hour Saturdays in July-September, shall not apply to employees on the Isthmus of Panama. Provisional, read from the transcription.

gaps.what: An accepted original printing of EO 1111 (needed for T2).
gaps.where_to_look: ProQuest/CIS Presidential Executive Orders and Proclamations replica of the State Department copy; NARA RG 11 numbered executive orders; Canal Zone executive order compilations (GPO) and the Canal Record, July 1909; Monthly Catalog entry at mocat.library.unt.edu/catalog/175-ch477 (HTTP 403 here) for the citation.

gaps.what: Whether and when EO 1096 (the parent) was expressly revoked or superseded. EO 1111 is an exemption from it and follows its status (rule d). Candidate only, it does not name the order as far as found: Saturday half-holiday Act of March 3, 1931.
gaps.where_to_look: The project's EO:1096 dossier; later civil-service hours orders of 1909-1945; the 1931 Act's text (46 Stat. 1482) for any repeal or supersession clause; Truman-era workweek orders.

gaps.what: Whether a later Canal Zone or Panama Canal instrument expressly revoked or superseded EO 1111 itself.
gaps.where_to_look: Executive Orders Relating to the Panama Canal (annotated compilations of 1921 and later); Canal Zone Code revision tables.

moves.note: Only a Wikisource transcription is held. No accepted original printing was located in the slice or by two web searches. A GPO Monthly Catalog entry (UNT mocat 175-ch477) appears to list the order but returned HTTP 403, and a catalog entry is not a printing of the text. The original is probably only in the State Department numbered series (ProQuest/CIS microfiche) or NARA RG 11, which would be OFFLINE.

propositions.claim: EO 1111 of 16 July 1909 has one operative sentence, exempting Isthmus of Panama employees from EO 1084 and EO 1096 (transcription, not an original).
propositions.quote: Executive Order No. 1084, made June 8, 1909, and Executive Order No. 1096, made June 25, 1909, shall have no application to employes upon the Isthmus of Panama.

propositions.claim: EO 1096 superseded EO 1084, so the exemption's live parent is EO 1096 (transcription).
propositions.quote: The following order will supersede that of June 8, 1909, as to hours of labor on Saturday during the months mentioned.

propositions.claim: EO 1096 runs each year 'until further notice', with no fixed end date in its own terms (transcription).
propositions.quote: during the months of July, August and September of each year until further notice, four hours, exclusive of time for luncheon, shall constitute a day's work on Saturdays

propositions.claim: EO 1084 also ran 'until further notice' and applied to all Federal employees wherever employed (transcription).
propositions.quote: until further notice, four hours, exclusive of time for luncheon, shall constitute a day's work for all employees in the Federal public service, wherever employed

review.conclusion_reason: OPEN and formal status unknown are warranted on the checked evidence: neither an ending nor positive current operation is established. Rule (d) supplies the parent-status inquiry identified in the gaps; the conclusion's basis_rule 'none' is imprecise. No accepted original was inspected, so the clause inventory remains provisional.

verdicts.reason: The held EO_1111.txt contains the quoted sole operative sentence and July 16, 1909 date. It is explicitly a Wikisource transcription.
EO_1096.txt contains the exact supersession sentence identifying the June 8, 1909 order. This supports EO 1096 as the relevant parent, not its continued operation at the cutoff.
EO_1096.txt contains the exact quoted annual recurrence and 'until further notice' language; its text supplies no fixed termination date.
EO_1084.txt contains the quoted 'until further notice' and 'wherever employed' language. The claim accurately describes the transcription.
